cues.text: Hi!
Find a comfortable position and let your body relax.
Take a slow breath in…
and breathe out.
Again, breathe in…
and slowly breathe out.
For the next few minutes, you don’t need to do anything for anyone.
This moment is yours.
All yours.
Today, we’re going to practice something that can feel surprisingly difficult: saying no.
Sometimes we say yes because we’re afraid of disappointing someone.
Sometimes we worry that the other person will think we’re rude, unfriendly, or difficult.
And when we’re speaking another language,
the fear can feel even stronger because we’re not always sure which words sound polite.
Take a deep breath in…
Saying no doesn’t always make you rude.
Sometimes, saying no simply means that you know what you want, what you need,
or what you’re ready for.
You can be kind to another person and still say no.
You can love someone and still say, “No, thank you.”
Now breathe out, and as you breathe out, let your shoulders relax a little more.
Imagine you’re sitting at a cozy restaurant.
There’s still some food on your plate, and you’re enjoying your meal.
A waiter comes to the table and asks, “Can I take your plate?” You’re not finished yet.
In this situation, saying only “no” sounds a bit direct.
The waiter is simply trying to help you, so you may want your answer a little softer,
a little more polite.
You can say, “Not yet, please.” Notice the word yet.
Not yet means not now, but maybe later.
You don’t want the waiter to take your plate now, but they can probably take it later.
You’re not rejecting the person.
You’re simply saying that you’re not ready yet.
And that's completely okay.
Breathe in…
Imagine yourself saying it calmly: “Not yet,
thanks.” You don’t need to apologize or give a long explanation.
You can simply smile, say what you need, and continue enjoying your meal.
You’ve communicated clearly and kindly.
You’ve done your part.
Now, let yourself feel confident in your answer.
You can say no without feeling guilty.
You can be kind while still respecting what you want.
Breathe out…
Notice how it feels to say what you want.
Now repeat quietly, either out loud or in your mind:
I can say no and still be kind.
I can be polite without saying yes.
I don’t always need to explain myself.
Take one more slow breath in…
and breathe out.
Let those words stay with you for a moment.
If something comes up in the next few days that you don’t want to do,
remember this moment.
Before you answer, take a breath and ask yourself: Do I really want to say yes,
or am I only saying yes because I’m afraid to say no?
Give yourself a moment to notice what you really want.
If your answer is no, you can say it politely and calmly.
You don’t need to feel guilty or worried just because someone may
have wanted a different answer.
After you say no, notice how you feel.
Maybe there’s a little discomfort at first.
That’s okay.
Let the feeling come and go without changing your answer.
Remind yourself: I was kind.
I was clear.
I respected what I needed.
And each time you practice saying no with kindness,
it can become a little easier and more natural.
Take one more slow breath in…
and gently breathe out.
Remember, saying no doesn’t mean you’re being unkind.
Sometimes, it simply means you’re listening to yourself.
You can be kind to others and still respect what you need.
So carry this thought with you:
I can say no calmly.
I can say no kindly.
And I can still feel at peace with my choice.
Take one final breath…
and when you’re ready, slowly open your eyes.
Thank you for taking this moment for yourself.
